segments.text: After every meal, cells in your gut release a hormone. It lasts about two minutes. Then an enzyme destroys it.
That hormone is G.L.P. one — glucagon-like peptide one. Thirty amino acids. It tells the pancreas to release insulin when blood sugar is high, and it reduces appetite in the brain.

A two-minute half-life is useless as medicine. The enzyme D.P.P. four chops the natural peptide almost immediately. To treat diabetes and obesity, we needed the same signal — in a structure that survives.
This is Omnigent, from Databricks. A meta-harness for A.I. agents. One shared session: web, desktop, or mobile. Policies, sandboxes, and live collaboration with Share.
We define Protein Lab in a short YAML file. Tools for Boltz structure prediction, stills, and spin movies. Change one line to swap the model harness — tools and guardrails stay the same.

In the session, the agent calls Boltz in the cloud. Sequence in. Coordinates and confidence out. For our G.L.P. one run: structure confidence zero point eight three. Complex P.L.D.D.T. zero point nine zero.

Here is the predicted fold. Natural G.L.P. one is gone in minutes. Engineered analogs keep the same fold family idea, resist D.P.P. four, and last for days — the science behind modern metabolic drugs.
In the Omnigent interface, tool cards stream as they run. The Agents panel shows the live worker. Contextual policies cap tool calls. Share lets a teammate watch the science unfold.
Sequence. Structure. Story. Protein Lab on Omnigent by Databricks. Run it with: omni run, agents, protein-lab.
